rounds.title: Make room for food
rounds.prompt: Which change should this landscape try first?

options.label: Plant native wildflower strips
options.description: Add seasonally varied forage along field edges.
options.note: The scenario models more available forage; it does not predict a real population change.

options.label: Mow less often in selected areas
options.description: Leave selected patches undisturbed for longer.
options.note: The scenario represents one possible management choice; timing and local conditions matter.

rounds.title: Create safe shelter
rounds.prompt: Where should the habitat make more room?

options.label: Keep some deadwood and old trees
options.description: Preserve a mix of natural nesting and overwintering places.
options.note: The EEA briefing describes deadwood and veteran trees as important for some pollinators.

options.label: Protect undisturbed soil patches
options.note: The EEA briefing notes that many wild bees nest below ground; the simulation is illustrative.

rounds.title: Make the landscape work together
rounds.prompt: What should link the habitat patches?

options.label: Connect semi-natural habitat patches
options.description: Build a more continuous route between habitat areas.
options.note: The EEA briefing emphasizes habitat diversity and connectivity at landscape scale.

options.label: Add a wider mix of flowering periods
options.description: Spread resources across more of the season.
options.note: This authored scenario models a diversified resource calendar; it is not a field forecast.

habitat.title: Protecting and restoring Europe’s wild pollinators and their habitats
habitat.supports: Habitat diversity and connectivity, wildflower strips, and pollinator-friendly management are among approaches discussed for supporting wild pollinators.

fao.title: Global Action on Pollination Services for Sustainable Agriculture
fao.publisher: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
fao.supports: Pollinators include a diversity of wild and managed species; their relationships to crops and ecosystems are broader than honeybees alone.

ivn-garden-guidance.title: Tuinieren: tips en inspiratie
ivn-garden-guidance.supports: Practical inspiration for choosing flowering plants and greening gardens for wildlife and neighbourhoods.

actions.title: Try one small wildlife-friendly change
actions.label: Explore garden ideas from IVN
actions.description: If you have a garden or shared green space, explore locally appropriate ways to provide varied flowering plants or shelter. This is optional; no purchase, pledge, or data collection is required.

resourceBudget.label: Fictional field tokens
resourceBudget.note: A game-only planning limit. Tokens are not money, materials, or a real restoration budget.
